reasoning: B has the better RL design. It uses step-based budgets so runs are reproducible, sets up a table-vs-network lesson for Snake, includes reward-hacking experiments, compares REINFORCE with PPO, and checks that the tank is hard enough and that predator-prey is balanced before any learning counts. Its opponent pool uses three game types so no rollout is wasted, it uses a cross-play table to tell progress from cycling, and its tests are concrete and numeric. But B carries a lot of edit history: superseded AD stubs, current decisions argued from superseded ones, '(changed 2026-10-15)' tags across the spec, and idea files that point at superseded decisions. It also has real cross-doc conflicts. The brief only describes Snake. GPU use is out of scope in the spec but a fallback in the architecture. CORE-01 is never extended to predator-prey. The brief says every environment must beat a random agent, but predator-prey has no random baseline. The whole set is also very long for a solo learner. A is lean, consistent and well organized, and has a clear build order and done gate per world. Its main flaws are in content. Wall-clock training budgets, a time-based epsilon schedule and time-based snapshot timing contradict its own determinism requirement (CORE-08). The tank and predator-prey physics have no numbers. A Snake DQN on the 11-fact view must beat a heuristic that uses the same 11 facts, and that risk is not flagged. SB3's DQN is not truly 'matched' to Double-DQN. On balance, A's cleaner and more usable documents outweigh B's deeper but inconsistent and bloated plan.

strengths: Compact three-doc set (about 750 lines) with no history residue and single-entry changelogs
Clean traceability: every component lists the requirement IDs it covers
Clear build order and gating: worlds are built in order, each gated by a done report, and the modules needed for Snake are listed
Sound PPO details: GAE, bootstrapping on time-outs, a policy shared per role, and agents that leave mid-episode
Covers all three worlds with baselines, significance tests (Holm-corrected families) and a reference check against an established library
Self-play section names the cycling risk and tests final vs earliest snapshots
weaknesses: Wall-clock budgets, a time-based epsilon schedule and time-based snapshot timing contradict the CORE-08 determinism requirement
Tank and predator-prey physics are underspecified: no speeds, sizes, catch or eating distances
Nothing checks that the tank's hand-written fish is beatable, or that predator-prey is balanced
Snake DQN on the 11-fact view must beat a heuristic that uses the same information; this risk is not flagged
Several tests are vague or circular (TANK-08, EVAL-02, RPLY-02)
Reward shaping, one of the user's stated concepts, is not explored

strengths: Pedagogically strong experiment design: table vs network, reward-hacking designs, REINFORCE vs PPO, simultaneous vs opponent-pool training
Very concrete, numeric acceptance tests (e.g. TANK-13 = 1,462.5, HUNT-13, 1.1 vs 1.3 sensing radii)
Careful RL reasoning: step-based budgets for reproducibility, truncation vs termination, a whole tank as one test sample, and swept-collision arithmetic
Opponent pool split into three game types so no rollout is wasted; cross-play tables plus cycling and forgetting reports
Gating checks (TEXP-01 tank difficulty, HEXP-01 balance) before any learning result counts
Learners never import environments, and a test enforces it; standard Gymnasium/PettingZoo faces support the later library comparison
weaknesses: Heavy history residue: superseded AD stubs, 'changed' tags throughout the spec, idea files describing past edits
Cross-doc conflicts: GPU out of scope vs GPU fallback; CORE-01 wording not extended to predator-prey; a brief that covers only Snake
Predator-prey lacks the random-baseline comparison the brief requires
Very long (about 1,350 lines including ideas) with some over-engineering (auto-profiling shrink ladder, PettingZoo face used only for a checker)
Plain-word stand-ins for standard terms ('situation estimate', 'policy spread') make it harder to map the text to RL literature
No explicit module build order for the first environment

A: spec.md: CORE-04 'it stops on its own within the budget' vs CORE-08 'when training runs twice, then the logged returns are identical'. Stopping on a wall-clock budget changes the episode count between reruns, so the two requirements contradict.

architecture.md AD-05: 'ε decays linearly from 1.0 to 0.05 over the first 30% of the budget'. The budget is wall-clock minutes, so exploration depends on machine timing and CORE-08 determinism breaks. The same applies to AD-07 'Each side snapshots 6 times, evenly across the budget'.
architecture.md AD-08: 'Settings are matched to AD-05 and AD-06'. Stable-Baselines3's DQN has no Double-DQN option, so it cannot match AD-05's 'Double-DQN targets'.
architecture.md AD-06: 'the defaults above match SB3's'. This is wrong for 'minibatch 256': SB3's PPO default batch_size is 64.

spec.md TANK-02/TANK-03: 'The ball moves at constant speed' / 'Each is limited to a fixed range'. No ball speed, fish speed, turn range, tank size or body radii are given, so difficulty and reaction time cannot be checked, and nothing confirms the hand-written fish can be beaten.
spec.md PRED-03: 'The predator's top speed is 1.2× a prey's'. No base speeds, catch distance or pellet-eating distance are given anywhere for predator-prey.
spec.md PRED-04: 'the predator: prey'. It is unclear whether animals still sense the wall and their own heading as in TANK-05.

spec.md VAL-05: 'A Snake agent trained with this method on the 11-fact observation passes EVAL-04' against the hand-written agent. The SNAKE-09 heuristic uses the same 11 facts, so the DQN has no information edge and may only tie it. The Risks section does not mention this.

architecture.md train_selfplay: 'for each side, opponent = current (p) or uniform snapshot (1-p); only sides playing their current policy record experience'. Independent draws per side make about 25% of rollouts snapshot vs snapshot, from which neither side learns.
spec.md PRED-10 / architecture.md AD-07: 'otherwise a snapshot picked at random'. Nothing says what happens before the first snapshot exists (taken at 1/6 of the budget).

architecture.md Risks: 'the cloud-computing fallback in the brief applies before any spec change'. QR-01 says 'on the learner's laptop CPU' and QR-05 requires CPU only, so moving to the cloud is itself a spec change.
spec.md TANK-08: 'Given fish that survived 1,000, 1,000 and 400 steps (and others)... then the score is the average across all 8'. The test gives no concrete expected value.
spec.md EVAL-02: 'then it behaves as the world section describes'. This test is circular.
spec.md RPLY-02: 'distinguishable at a glance'. This test is subjective.
spec.md PRED-11: 'rejects H0 each time against the matching snapshot of the prey'. The comparison is hard to parse in the spec; only the architecture makes it clear.
brief.md / spec.md: rewards are fixed per world ('PRED-05 Prey rewards', 'TANK-06'). Reward shaping, one of the user's stated learning concepts, is never studied.

architecture.md Project layout: 'The tank adds ... and extends `core` for continuous actions and several agents'. The Interfaces section already defines Box actions, roles and multi-agent dicts up front, so it is unclear what 'extends' means.
B: architecture.md: 'AD-02: ~~Gymnasium environment format~~ Status: Superseded by AD-14' and 'AD-10: ~~Batched agents and a batch face for every environment~~ Superseded by AD-13'. Superseded decisions are kept as stubs.
architecture.md AD-13 Context: 'AD-10 gave every environment a batch face for one shared policy'. A current decision is argued from a superseded one.
architecture.md AD-14 Context: 'AD-02 chose Gymnasium for every environment's standard face'. A current decision is argued from a superseded one.

spec.md: '*(changed 2026-10-15)*' tags on CORE-01, CORE-02, CORE-04, BASE-01, BASE-03, PG-06, EVAL-01, EVAL-02, VIEW-01–VIEW-03, NOTE-01, DATA-02, QR-01 and QR-04. This is edit-history residue in a spec where every change is dated the same day.
architecture.md AD-13: 'Snake, the corridor and the tank change only in name ("main"). Nothing is built yet.' This describes a change against an earlier design, not the current design.
architecture.md AD-15: 'The tank code is refactored to use envs.disk. Nothing is built yet, so this costs nothing.' Same problem: it describes a change against an earlier design.

spec.md CORE-01: 'Given the Snake environment or the tank, when it is checked with an established library's environment checker'. AD-14 says 'CORE-01 now also covers predator–prey', but the requirement and its test were never extended to it, and the predator-prey changelog row omits CORE-01.

spec.md Out of scope: 'Any run that needs a GPU'. This contradicts architecture AD-04 'Rented cloud GPU — allowed by the brief, but kept only as a fallback' and the Risks line 'and only then a rented GPU'.

brief.md: success and bets cover only Snake ('In Snake, I have seen a lookup table of move values break down', 'A value-learning agent can beat the rule-based Snake player'). The tank, predator-prey, policy gradients and co-evolution never appear, and ideas/predator-prey.md says 'Brief changes: none.'

brief.md Goal 3: 'Each environment is built around one main concept' is followed by 'Snake comes first: learning move values, how what the agent sees shapes learning, and how badly designed rewards get exploited'. That is three concepts for one environment.

brief.md: 'For each environment, the trained agent clearly beats both a random agent and a simple hand-written rule-based player'. HEXP-02/03 compare only against scripted players; predator-prey has no random-player comparison (spec Summary: 'where it makes sense, a random player').

ideas/predator-prey.md: 'the setup shrinks (fewer fish, shorter games or fewer generations)'. The spec's HEXP-05 ladder has no 'fewer fish' step, and it adds fewer cross-play games and fewer training steps.
ideas/predator-prey.md: 'Architecture AD-10 assumes one policy per batch.' This points at a superseded decision.

ideas/fish-tank.md: 'CORE-04 and QR-04, which still need the change from architecture AD-09' and 'worded for Snake games and food scores'. Both are stale: the change is already applied and the wording already generalised.
ideas/fish-tank.md: 'This is my proposed limit, for you to check.' Draft conversation text is left in a doc marked 'Specced'.

spec.md Out of scope: 'Designing the shared core up front for environments not yet built'. None of the three environments is built, and AD-13 designs the core for all three; this is leftover framing from a Snake-only plan.
spec.md DQN-04: 'The replay memory and the target copy can each be switched off for an experiment'. No EXP experiment uses either switch, so the feature has no planned use or check.
architecture.md AD-07: 'MP4 — needs ffmpeg installed on the system'. imageio-ffmpeg installs its own ffmpeg binary through pip, so this reason for rejecting MP4 is wrong.
architecture.md Cross-cutting: 'The M1 has 8 cores.' The chip model is not given; the user only said Apple Silicon.

spec.md + architecture.md: 463 + 689 lines, 16 feature areas, an auto-profiling shrink ladder (AD-17) and a PettingZoo face used only for a checker. This is heavy for a solo evenings-and-weekends lab.
